tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with an imperative instruction ('Run a read-only...' and 'Use when asked to assess, audit, or review...'), focuses on user intent (assessing SageMaker security posture), lists explicit trigger contexts (notebook exposure, KMS encryption, model isolation, GuardDuty coverage, MLOps governance, etc.), and clarifies the output and boundaries while remaining a tight paragraph.
tests.evidence: "Use when asked to assess, audit, or review the security of Amazon SageMaker AI workloads: notebook and domain direct-internet exposure and VPC-only deployment, notebook instance privileged-access settings, KMS encryption at rest..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is concise and focuses on project-specific conventions (verifiability classification, read-only enforcement, check IDs, report assembly) rather than explaining general concepts the agent already knows (e.g., it doesn't explain what SageMaker or KMS encryption is in general terms).
tests.evidence: "Verify vs. prescribe (determinism contract)" section describes a specific, non-obvious classification scheme (Verifiable/Heuristic/Prescribe-only) unique to this skill rather than generic explanation.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body does not embed the 25-check catalog or report schema details; it defers those to references/sagemaker-checks.md and references/finding-schema-and-report.md, keeping only orchestration logic in the body.
tests.evidence: "it is the authoritative catalog of all 25 checks (`SM-01`..`SM-25`), each with the read-only API call(s), pass/fail/N-A logic, severity, verifiability, resolution text, and a documentation link." is a pointer, not inlined data.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Both reference files are linked with proper markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link specifies a clear trigger/condition for when to load it (Step 3 before running checks, Steps 2/4/5 for region resolution and report format).
tests.evidence: "Load [references/sagemaker-checks.md](references/sagemaker-checks.md) in Step 3, before running any check" and "Load [references/finding-schema-and-report.md](references/finding-schema-and-report.md) in Steps 2, 4, and 5"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/consistency-critical operations (read-only enforcement, verifiability contract, schema conformance) are given exact, prescriptive rules, while flexible aspects (how to run checks per region/account) are described with enough latitude; this matches fragility to prescriptiveness well.
tests.evidence: "NEVER call any API that creates, updates, deletes, attaches, enables, disables, or otherwise mutates a resource" is appropriately strict for a safety-critical constraint.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tools/approaches as menus; it specifies exact read-only API verb classes and a single reference catalog to follow, avoiding tool-choice ambiguity.
tests.evidence: No multiple-approach menu is presented; the skill mandates "ONLY call Describe*, List*, Get*, BatchGet*" as the single approach.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (resolve accounts/regions, run checks per region/account, assemble report, self-check) rather than a one-off task declaration, applicable to any SageMaker security assessment request.
tests.evidence: "Step 3 — Run the SageMaker checks per region... execute every check" generalizes across any account/region scope, not tied to a specific instance.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated 'Notes and limitations' section plus a detailed verify-vs-prescribe contract and multi-account/region caveats that function as gotchas, covering non-obvious pitfalls like IAM detection limits and SM-02 mixed verifiability.
tests.evidence: "`SM-02` is a mixed check... Do not call `Generate*`, report those aspects as prescribe guidance in the resolution."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly defers the output format/template definition to references/finding-schema-and-report.md, so a template exists but is appropriately kept out of the body.
tests.evidence: "it defines region and account resolution, the exact finding schema, and the consolidated report format."

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the report format is fully delegated to the reference file.
